text.p: John B. Sanfilippo & Son Inc, which posted a narrowed loss in the first quarter, said Monday it expects a "good" 1997.
Earlier, it reported a first quarter net loss of $0.02 a share, compared with a year-ago loss of $0.13. Sales rose 10.3 percent to $58.5 million.

"...(T)he minimal loss reported is what we expected and I am pleased with 1997's start after a very disappointing 1996," Chairman Jasper Sanfilippo said in a statement. "Based upon the first quarter's start, the company's senior management and I look ahead to a good 1997."

Improved retail and food service sales increased the first quarter gross margin to 16.3 percent from 15.4 percent a year ago. Selling and administrative expenses totaled 13.6 percent of net sales, down from 14.4 percent in the year-ago quarter, the company said.
Operating income improved to approximately $1.6 million, or 2.8 percent of net sales in the first quarter, from $534,000 or one percent of net sales a year ago.
John B. Sanfilippo processes, packages, markets and distributes shelled and in-shell nuts and sesame sticks.
